title: Quadratic Equations
summary: A quadratic $ax^2+bx+c=0$ can be solved by factoring (zero-product), the square-root property, completing the square, or the quadratic formula $x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$. The discriminant $b^2-4ac$ tells how many real solutions exist.

zero-product property.plain: A product is zero only if a factor is zero.
zero-product property.in_class: Factor, then set each factor to 0.

quadratic formula.plain: The solution formula for any quadratic.

vertex.plain: The turning point of the parabola.

roots.plain: The solutions — where the parabola meets the $x$-axis.

concept_sections.heading: Solving by factoring
concept_sections.explanation: If the quadratic factors, set it to zero, factor, and apply the zero-product property: each factor equal to zero gives a solution.
math_steps: Set each factor to 0 and solve.

concept_sections.heading: The square-root property
concept_sections.explanation: For $x^2=k$ (or $(x-h)^2=k$), take the square root of both sides, remembering the $\pm$: $x=\pm\sqrt k$.

concept_sections.heading: Completing the square
concept_sections.explanation: Turn $x^2+bx$ into a perfect square by adding $(b/2)^2$ to both sides, then use the square-root property. This also derives the quadratic formula.
math_steps: Factor the perfect square and take roots.

concept_sections.heading: The quadratic formula
concept_sections.explanation: For any $ax^2+bx+c=0$, $x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$. It always works — plug in $a,b,c$ carefully with signs.

concept_sections.heading: The discriminant
concept_sections.explanation: The sign of $b^2-4ac$ tells the solution count: positive ⇒ two real, zero ⇒ one (repeated), negative ⇒ two complex.

real_world_examples.title: Projectile height
real_world_examples.scenario: A ball's height is quadratic in time.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Setting height to zero and solving finds when it lands — a quadratic equation.

real_world_examples.title: Maximizing area
real_world_examples.scenario: A fixed fence enclosing the most area.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The area is a quadratic; its vertex gives the optimal dimensions.

real_world_examples.title: Golden-ratio design
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The defining proportion leads to a quadratic solved by the formula.
